newsitem.title: PERU: Mild quake shakes Peru's south coast, no damage.
newsitem.headline: Mild quake shakes Peru's south coast, no damage.

text.p: A mild earthquake struck Peru's southern coast early on Tuesday, rattling windows and waking residents but apparently causing no casualties or damage, officials said.

A quake measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale, with an epicentre in the Pacific Ocean 60 miles (100 kms) southwest of Ica, jolted the country's southern coast at 5:35 a.m. (1035 GMT), said Henry Moncada of the Geophysical Institute of Peru.
"At this point, we have no reports of injuries," he told Reuters.
The temblor was centred 22 miles (35.5 kms) under the Earth's surface. The quake's precise duration was not immediately known but it "apparently was short," Moncada said.
Ica is on the coast 150 miles (240 kms) south of Lima. Local radio said the tremor also was felt in the nearby town of Chincha.
